scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen short northwestern opening
correspondence.finding: The opening lies in the mapped intermittent headward-channel approach west of the directly labeled Little Bernard Creek reach. The original shows its channel connection into the eastward creek corridor near the Pless/Track Road and Plum Creek Road surroundings. This short approach has no independently established local name and is not asserted to be the natural source of a named river. Ordinary generalization and a local offset do not interrupt the mapped corridor.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: Western initial portion of part 0 only.

correspondence.component_scope: Little Bernard Creek eastward and southward corridor
correspondence.finding: Little Bernard Creek is directly labeled on the mapped eastward channel and again on its southward continuation by Rexville. The selected route follows that corridor, crosses the I-10/US90 setting and continues south. Small adjacent water polygons and Hog Branch remain separately mapped features; their proximity is not used to invent a through-lake route.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: Named portion of part 0 and northern part of part 1; exact naming-transition point is unverified.

correspondence.component_scope: East Bernard Creek and San Bernard joining setting
correspondence.finding: The source labels the southward and southeastern channel below Rexville as East Bernard Creek. The mapped lower creek receives the distinct Hog Branch approach and continues to its direct junction with the San Bernard River near the FM1093 setting. All selected intervening joins are covered. East Bernard Creek and Little Bernard Creek are retained as separately displayed reach names, not declared formal aliases.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: Southern part of part 1 and parts 2–3; exact hydronym boundary is not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: San Bernard River from the East Bernard Creek junction through East Bernard and Kendleton
correspondence.finding: The mapped San Bernard River is directly and repeatedly labeled along the southeastward floodplain below the joining creek. The selected route corresponds to its bends south of Wallis, east of the city of East Bernard, through the Kendleton/US59 crossing and onward past the West Bernard Creek joining setting. Nearby Brazos River, canals and distinct tributary corridors are separately visible and are not substituted for the chosen river.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle San Bernard and Newgulf reservoir/canal surroundings
correspondence.finding: The readable originals cover the whole selected middle corridor, its intermediate joins and the meandering San Bernard through the Newgulf setting. Large irregular and rectangular waterbodies, levees and side canals occur beside the river, while the river channel remains visibly connected around them. The generalized selected route follows that river corridor; no independent lake or reservoir through-passage, reservoir name assignment, pumping connection or flow operation is needed or claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower inland San Bernard through the West Columbia/Sweeny surroundings
correspondence.finding: The sources show a connected named San Bernard corridor south through wooded lowland, tributary and wetland settings, then east past the Sweeny/El Bernardo surroundings. The selected turns and joins correspond to this river at ordinary corridor scale. San Bernard Reservoir Number 2 and nearby ponds/canals are shown beside the river and retain their distinct geographic role; the selected line is not treated as evidence of an axial passage through that reservoir.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower San Bernard coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The original shows the San Bernard continuing southeast through the residential/road setting, the Churchill vicinity and the increasingly broad wetland/coastal corridor. All selected portions through these bends are covered by a visible connected river. McNeal Lake, Pelican Lake and nearby bayous are separately mapped coastal waters rather than alternative names for the selected river.

correspondence.component_scope: Intracoastal Waterway junction/crossing and actual open-coast ending
correspondence.finding: The named San Bernard reaches the directly mapped Intracoastal Waterway and continues south across that joining/crossing setting to the open-coast inlet. The actual final selected approach and endpoint lie in this mapped coastal outlet corridor. The original enlargement shows the water connection beyond the waterway rather than merely a nearby coastal label. Intracoastal Waterway remains a separate managed-water feature; no present flow direction, mouth maintenance, sediment state or exact shore/bank vertex is established.

correspondence.component_scope: western_headward_stream_and_lake_approach
correspondence.finding: The initial selected stream, small connected waters, northward passage and eastward turn correspond to the mapped feeder corridor west and northwest of Burns Lake. The source distinguishes this passage from nearby parallel lake chains and shows its approach to the lake. No feeder hydronym, surveyed ultimate source or current flow state is established.

correspondence.component_scope: burns_lake_inlet_and_passage
correspondence.finding: The eastward feeder enters the northwestern end of the large irregular lake explicitly labeled Burns Lake. The selected southward passage, central lake body and southeastern outlet are visible. The name is retained for this lake component only; its occurrence in the sheet title is not used to name the river group.

correspondence.component_scope: burns_outlet_and_eastward_upper_river
correspondence.finding: The original shows the southeastern Burns Lake outlet entering a substantial eastward channel, including small intervening waters and material northern and southern stream arrivals. The distinct southeast and east bends match the selected corridor at the source scale. No river name is printed along this selected interval.

correspondence.component_scope: middle_eastward_channel_and_southern_turn
correspondence.finding: The eastward channel, subsequent southeast descent, southern bend and northeast turn are continuously depicted with the selected intervening lakes, widenings and stream junctions. Thematic management boundaries are distinguishable from the watercourse and are not treated as hydrographic links.

correspondence.component_scope: northeastern_lake_and_channel_succession
correspondence.finding: The selected northeastward passage follows the mapped elongated lakes and connecting channels, including their islands, narrow joins, side-stream arrivals and the long lake immediately before the lower eastward outlet. Individual lake names are not established. Nearby numerical lake elevations and fish-resource symbols are not names.

correspondence.component_scope: last_large_lake_outlet_and_lower_eastward_reach
correspondence.finding: The northern end of the final elongated lake connects to the mapped eastward river, which receives the separate western/northern lake outlet and then curves northeast. The original accounts for the selected larger bends and material junctions without requiring exact bank or vertex agreement.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_northward_river_and_sheet_crossing
correspondence.finding: The lower river turns north/northeast beside small lakes and tributaries and continues across the Burns Lake eastern neatline. The adjoining Cape Stang original depicts the same west-side coastal approach and lower channel. No cross-sheet geographic gap remains at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: actual_terminal_and_receiving_bay
correspondence.finding: The selected final reach enters the western shore of the inlet labeled Hadley Bay. The original lower-channel and shoreline connection is visible just east of the shared sheet edge. It is a separate outlet from the larger river and lake passage reaching the bay farther southeast. The bay name is receiving-water context, not a river name or claim about the precise modern shoreline.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and initial feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in the mapped Quixadá-side drainage west of Ibaretama and southwest of Boa Vista. The original shows the eastward local stream, small adjoining waterbodies, the settlement/road-crossing setting and the northward continuation into the Cipó approach. The opening is a chosen point on that mapped drainage, not an independently established natural source. No name is supplied for this initial feeder and no nearby pond name is invented.

correspondence.component_scope: Riacho do Cipó approach and Pirangi junction
correspondence.finding: The mapped stream bends northeast and east past the Riacho do Cipó label, then turns northeast along the Boa Vista-side corridor and joins the west-arriving Rio Pirangi near the western Ibaretama boundary. The separate Riacho da Ema and Açude Olho D’Água approach remain contextual northern branches. The selected Cipó approach is not renamed as the whole upper Pirangi, and no exact naming boundary is asserted.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Riacho do Cipó (directly labelled component only)

correspondence.component_scope: Pirangi through Triunfo, Piranji and the São Francisco approach
correspondence.finding: The western direct Rio Pirangi label and the joined continuous corridor are followed northeast past Triunfo, the Piranji settlement and its northern/western tributary joins, then east beside Santa Clara toward São Francisco and the Nova Vida/Aroeira setting. The nearby Riacho da Lagoa, other side streams and small waterbodies are depicted separately. The selected route stays on the receiving river corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Açude Batente approach, through-waterbody passage and outlet
correspondence.finding: Overlapping municipal originals show the Pirangi approach past Caiçara/Quinxinxé into the long southwestern arm, the connected main waterbody, the separate northwestern Riacho do Mosquito arm and the eastward outlet toward Curralinho. The enlarged Ocara original reads Açude Batente. The selected route crosses this distinct impoundment and continues along the eastern river; the reservoir is not a river-name alias. No present operation, hydraulic transfer or current shoreline is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern Pirangi and Ocara–Morada Nova corridor
correspondence.finding: The mapped river continues east and northeast from the Batente outlet through the Curralinho and Zacarias settings, past the developed settlement west of the Lagoa do Bode label, then north along the repeatedly labelled Pirangi corridor. Riacho Pixota and Riacho do Serrote are side joins. The Ocara and Beberibe sheets overlap across the same bends and the southern Beberibe approach, closing the municipal-map seam.

correspondence.component_scope: Road/canal crossing setting, Poço Medeiros and northward bend
correspondence.finding: The selected river is followed across the main diagonal road near Tapuio/Santa Maria, north past Grossos and Poço Medeiros, and around the bends toward Cruz and Cedro. The map separately labels Canal da Integração and depicts its adjoining/crossing setting; the selected through-corridor is the Pirangi river, not the canal. No canal-operation or current-flow assertion is needed for this bounded cartographic identity. Córrego Gaim and Córrego das Cabras are distinguished from the main river, which turns east near Cedro.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward lower Pirangi and widened lower-river passage
correspondence.finding: The continuous lower corridor is followed east from Cedro/Boa Vista past Jatobá and Andresa to Itapeim, then via Arataca, Encruzilhada and Várzea da Serra into the broad connected lower-river waterbody near Carnaúba Torta, Pirangi locality and Caroé. The mapped side connections and lower widening are visible; no separate lake or reservoir name is established for that widening. The route then continues east toward the Parajuru meanders. Separate southern drainage and lagoon names are not extended to the selected through-water.

correspondence.component_scope: Parajuru estuary and actual Atlantic ending
correspondence.finding: Direct Rio Pirangi labels identify the lower meanders south of Parajuru/Recanto. The connected coastal channel beside Praia do Parajuru and the adjacent labelled Atlantic establish the selected terminal receiving setting. This is the Pirangi/Parajuru mouth corridor, distinct from the Jaguaribe estuary farther southeast and the separate Córrego de Maceió. The rendered terminal is treated at ordinary coastal-corridor scale, without claiming a surveyed mouth, a particular present tidal branch, or exact agreement with the historical shoreline.
correspondence.bounded_component_name: Rio Pirangi estuarine corridor; Oceano Atlântico receiving water

correspondence.component_scope: Opening near Miguel Hidalgo / Estación Laguna Seca and southern plain
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on the plain in the Miguel Hidalgo and Estación Laguna Seca setting. Its northward course passes the Aquiles Serdán, Francisco I. Madero and Santa Cruz del Mogote settings. The original depicts nearby intermittent arroyos, small water bodies and tanks, but does not establish this selected north-going through-channel. Nearby Arroyo Colorado, Arroyo el Chamorro and the small Miguel Hidalgo waterbody are not assigned to the opening or converted into a selected lake crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: La Maroma, Wadley and Estación Catorce plain and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: All selected parts traverse the plain beside the railway and road corridor west of the Sierra de Catorce. The map separately labels local intermittent courses including A. el Boquerón, Arroyo de Jesús, A. las Tapias, A. la Matanza and Arroyo Don Emeterio. They approach or cross the plain in differing directions; stream-disappearance symbols occur in this setting. The original does not join them into the selected longitudinal passage from La Maroma through Wadley to Estación Catorce. These adjacent names remain contextual rather than supported selected reach names.

correspondence.component_scope: Loreto–Vanegas passage and overlap into northern municipal mapping
correspondence.finding: The selection continues past Loreto and the Vanegas railway/road setting. Both originals expose the municipal overlap and the crossing El Mezquital corridor. The topographic sheet labels Arroyo el Mezquital on a separate approach from the western hills; the municipal hydrography table identifies El Mezquital as intermittent. Neither source makes that label the name of the long selected northbound feature or establishes the full preceding and following plain connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Vanegas plain through the Papagayos–La Borrada setting
correspondence.finding: The municipal Relieve map covers every selected part north of the topographic-sheet boundary. It shows the broad plain, local hill margins and several separate east-west and diagonal drainage lines. The selected passage northward between those mapped approaches is not shown as a demonstrably connected single channel. Ordinary municipal cartographic generalization is acknowledged; the unresolved through-links remain a material source gap rather than a declaration that no local drainage exists.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northeastward parts, northern Vanegas plain and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The actual ending is in the northern Vanegas plain, south of the mapped El Coyote waterbody, within the Vanegas municipal footprint. It is not moved to the waterbody label, to the northern municipal boundary, or to a river in neighboring Galeana. The Relieve map supplies the terminal plain and nearby drainage setting, but not a demonstrated selected through-link from the preceding plain or a confirmed named receiving lake at the model endpoint. Galeana mapping is boundary context only.
